  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The "make the same tick in it" re-tick copies a tick onto a newer pipeline comment by step title, without checking that the newer entry's instructions or source SHA still match the verified step.
  WHY: `scripts/operator_step_issue.py` `upsert` (lines 342-361) appends a new entry whenever the rendered entry changes, so a changed step with the same title could be marked done without verification. - .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:87; workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:96 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The command copies a tick to a newer entry based on its step title, without verifying that the newer entry's instructions still match the work that was confirmed.
  WHY: `scripts/operator_step_issue.py:342-361` appends a new entry comment when an upsert's rendered entry changes. A newer entry with the same title but changed instructions would be marked complete without verification.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:87 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The re-tick is unconditional and title-scoped only. `upsert` appends a new entry comment whenever the newest entry differs from a freshly rendered one (lines 360-361). The command never compares the newer entry's instructions or its `<!-- ai:operator-step:source-sha=... -->` line against the verified runbook step.
  WHY: A newer entry with changed instruction B would show as done without being executed or verified, since `_authoritative_entry_comments` (`scripts/operator_step_issue.py:376-390`) reads only the newest entry. The "Never tick a step that was not verified" guard does not cover this. Suggested mitigation: re-tick only when the newer entry's instructions or source SHA match the verified step.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:96 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Same unconditional "same tick" defect as in the live copy.
  WHY: Identical to the live copy.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:87 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The unconditional re-tick of a concurrently arriving higher-id comment is the same defect, seen through the race lens. The superseding-comment window can carry a stale verification onto new entry content.
  WHY: `upsert` appends a new comment on any rendered-entry difference, which is the concurrent-write case this bullet targets.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
